title: Detection of monothioformic acid towards the solar-type protostar IRAS 16293─2422
question: Search for and characterize the rotational emission lines of the SH-bearing molecule monothioformic acid (t-HC(O)SH) and other SH-bearing molecules towards the solar-type protostar IRAS 16293 B.

what.value: Molecular spectroscopy catalog entries for t-HC(O)SH (CDMS entry 062515) and other SH-bearing molecules

evidence.loc: Identification of emission lines of t-HC(O)SH towards the IRAS 16293 B
evidence.quote: We used the local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) model with the Cologne Database for Molecular Spectroscopy (CDMS) to identify the molecular emission lines of t-HC(O)SH (CDMS entry 062515) towards the IRAS 16293 B (cite: mu05).

what.value: Column density of molecular H2 towards IRAS 16293 B (1.20x10^25 cm^-2)

evidence.loc: Fractional abundance of t-HC(O)SH towards the IRAS 16293 B
evidence.quote: The fractional abundance of t-HC(O)SH with respect to H$_{2}$ towards the IRAS 16293 B is 8.50$\times$10$^{-11}$, while the column density of molecular H$_{2}$ towards the IRAS 16293 B is 1.20$\times$10$^{25}$ cm$^{-2}$ (cite: jo16; cou18).

what.value: Column density (5.5x10^15 cm^-2) and abundance (4.58x10^-10) of CH3SH towards IRAS 16293 B

evidence.loc: Fractional abundance of t-HC(O)SH towards the IRAS 16293 B
evidence.quote: The fractional abundance of t-HC(O)SH towards the IRAS 16293 B with respect to another SH–bearing molecule, CH$_{3}$SH is 0.185, where the column density of CH$_{3}$SH towards the IRAS 16293 B is 5.5$\times$10$^{15}$ cm$^{-2}$ (cite: dro18).

evidence.loc: Fractional abundance of t-HC(O)SH towards the IRAS 16293 B
evidence.quote: Our derived fractional abundance of t-HC(O)SH (8.50$\times$10$^{-11}$) is lower than the abundance of CH$_{3}$SH (4.58$\times$10$^{-10}$)[^5].

what.value: Fractional abundance of t-HC(O)SH towards G+0.693–0.027 (1.2x10^-10) and G31.41+0.31 (1.4x10^-8)

evidence.loc: Fractional abundance of t-HC(O)SH towards the IRAS 16293 B
evidence.quote: Earlier, (cite: rod21) and (cite: gar22) detected the rotational emission lines of t-HC(O)SH from G+0.693–0.027 and G31.41+0.31, with an estimated fractional abundance 1.2$\times$10$^{-10}$ and 1.4$\times$10$^{-8}$ respectively.

recipe.goal: Calibrate raw visibility data, split target, and image continuum and spectral cubes
recipe.method: Calibrate visibilities with the ALMA pipeline in CASA 5.4.1 using SETJY (Perley-Butler 2017), hifa_bandpassflag, and hifa_flagdata; split target with MSTRANSFORM; image continuum with TCLEAN; subtract continuum with UVCONTSUB; image cubes with TCLEAN; correct primary beam with IMPBCOR.
key_parameters: Briggs weighting robust = 0.5, SPECMODE=CUBE, hogbom deconvolver

recipe.goal: Measure 1.274 mm continuum flux densities of IRAS 16293 A and B
recipe.method: Fit 2D Gaussians over the continuum emission image of sources IRAS 16293 A and IRAS 16293 B using CASA task IMFIT.

recipe.goal: Extract molecular spectra towards IRAS 16293 B and perform baseline correction
recipe.method: Extract molecular emission spectra from the continuum-subtracted spectral cubes using a 2.07'' diameter circular aperture centered on IRAS 16293 B, and fit a first-order polynomial for baseline correction using the GNU R package hyperSpec.
key_parameters: Circular region diameter = 2.07'' centered at RA (J2000) = 16h32m22s.603, Dec (J2000) = –24d28'32''.729; first-order polynomial baseline

recipe.goal: Identify t-HC(O)SH transitions and fit LTE model parameters, and derive upper limits for other SH-bearing species
recipe.method: Model extracted spectra assuming LTE in CASSIS with CDMS spectroscopy (entry 062515 for t-HC(O)SH) using the MCMC algorithm via the Python script interface; model >200 other molecules to check for line blending; estimate LTE upper limit column densities for 13 other SH-bearing species.
key_parameters: Source size = 0.5'', V_LSR = 2.7 km s^-1, CDMS entry 062515
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), T_c = 0, cosmic background temperature T_bg = 2.73 K

recipe.goal: Calculate fractional abundance of t-HC(O)SH relative to H2 and CH3SH
recipe.method: Divide the derived column density of t-HC(O)SH by the literature column densities of H2 and CH3SH towards IRAS 16293 B.
assumptions: N(H2) = 1.20x10^25 cm^-2 (cite: jo16; cou18) and N(CH3SH) = 5.5x10^15 cm^-2 (cite: dro18)

recipe.goal: Create moment zero maps and measure emitting region sizes of t-HC(O)SH
recipe.method: Generate integrated emission maps (moment zero) for three non-blended lines using CASA task IMMOMENTS, fit 2D Gaussians with IMFIT, and compute deconvolved source size theta_S = sqrt(theta_50^2 - theta_beam^2).
key_parameters: Transitions at 234.001 GHz, 234.021 GHz, and 234.074 GHz
